newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil deputies uphold oil bill's Petrobras clause.
newsitem.headline: Brazil deputies uphold oil bill's Petrobras clause.

text.p: Brazil's Chamber of Deputies upheld a clause included in a bill regulating the country's petroleum sector which says oil and gas giant Petrobras must remain in state hands.
In a show of hands, the lower house rejected a proposed amendment to the bill which would have eliminated the clause.

The amendment had been presented by members of the government-allied Liberal Front Party who wanted to undo an agreement undertaken by President Fernando Henrique Cardoso in 1995 that Petrobras would not be privatized.
Cardoso made that pledge to win support in the Senate for a constitutional amendment which did away with the Brazilian state's monopoly over several areas of the oil and gas industries.
The Chamber of Deputies approved a bill regulating that amendment last week and was voting Tuesday on a series of proposed amendments to the legislation.
Before defeating the amendment which would have allowed Petrobras to be privatized, the lower house approved another amendment which alters rules on fuel distribution.

The amended version of the bill gives licensed distributors virtually exclusive rights to distribution of fuel and natural gas during a five-year transition period. After five years consumers may purchase fuel and gas direct from refineries.
During the transition period, however, steelmakers, petrochemical and chemical companies and thermoelectric power units may buy directly from producers.
Once voting on the amendments is completed, probably later on Tuesday, the bill advances to the Senate.

The legislation allows private companies to compete or enter joint ventures with Petrobras, creates the National Petroleum Agency as a new regulator and does away with fuel price subsidies within three years.
